common_name: Penny's Pink Hellebore (Clear Pink Lenten Rose)

planting.note: Plant container-grown hellebores in fall or early spring in deep shade under deciduous trees; in zone 9 plant October-February. Hellebores resent transplanting once established, so choose the permanent site carefully. Penny's Pink flowers December-March in zone 9, when little else in the garden is blooming.

directions: Plant in shade to partial shade in well-drained, humus-rich, slightly alkaline to neutral, consistently moist soil, siting hellebores where cool root conditions and good drainage protect against crown rot. Penny's Pink is a named Lenten rose hybrid selected for abundant, clear rose-pink outward-facing flowers held on relatively upright stems, making the blooms easier to appreciate without kneeling down and peering underneath the foliage the way many nodding-flowered hellebores require. Leathery, deeply lobed, dark evergreen foliage provides structure in the shade garden year-round, and the winter to early-spring bloom period supplies color and early forage for bumblebees when few other perennials are active. Established clumps are long-lived and slowly expand; leave undisturbed for best flowering, and simply cut back tattered old foliage in late winter just as new flower stems emerge.
sources: North Carolina State University Extension — Hellebore for Southern Gardens

planting.note: Plant container-grown hellebores in fall or early spring in deep shade under deciduous trees; in zone 9 plant October-February. Cinnamon Snow flowers December-March in zone 9, providing winter color when little else blooms.

directions: Plant in shade to partial shade in well-drained, humus-rich, slightly alkaline to neutral, consistently moist soil. Cinnamon Snow is part of breeder Marietta O'Byrne's Winter Jewels strain of Lenten rose, selected for creamy white outward-facing flowers brushed and speckled with cinnamon-pink and rose tones that deepen with age, giving each bloom a distinctive warm, spice-toned overlay on its white base. Like other Winter Jewels selections it is grown from carefully hand-pollinated seed strains rather than tissue culture, so individual plants show some natural variation while sharing the strain's characteristic vigor, heavy bloom count, and well-held, outward-facing flower form. The leathery, deeply cut evergreen foliage provides year-round structure, and established clumps bloom more heavily each year if left undisturbed; simply remove tattered old leaves in late winter as the new flower stems emerge.
sources: Northwest Garden Nursery — Winter Jewels Hellebore Strain

common_name: Double Ellen Picotee Hellebore (Double-Flowered Picotee Lenten Rose)

planting.note: Plant container-grown hellebores in fall or early spring in deep shade under deciduous trees; in zone 9 plant October-February. Double Ellen Picotee flowers December-March in zone 9.

directions: Plant in shade to partial shade in well-drained, humus-rich, slightly alkaline to neutral, consistently moist soil. Double Ellen Picotee belongs to the Double Ellen strain of Lenten rose bred by Marietta O'Byrne for full, rounded, fully double flowers reminiscent of small camellias rather than the simple five-petaled form of species hellebores, and this selection shows pale petals crisply edged in a contrasting rose-purple picotee margin. The layered double flowers hold their form and color for many weeks in late winter and early spring, well outlasting many other winter bloomers, and the deeply cut, leathery evergreen foliage gives the shade garden structure through the rest of the year. Established plants resent disturbance, so choose a permanent shaded site with good drainage; groom off old winter-worn leaves in late winter just as the new flower stems emerge for the cleanest display.
sources: Northwest Garden Nursery — Double Ellen Hellebore Strain

planting.note: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Paradigm holds its gold center best with some morning sun but scorches in hot afternoon exposure.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, giving some protection from hot afternoon sun to prevent leaf scorch on the gold center. Paradigm produces large, heavily corrugated leaves with a bright gold center that brightens as the season progresses, bordered by an irregular, wide, blue-green margin that gives strong two-tone contrast in the shade border. Pale lavender flowers appear on scapes held above the foliage in summer, though the mounding, boldly colored foliage is the main attraction. Like other large hostas it forms a substantial, slow-expanding clump over several years and benefits from division in spring only when the clump becomes crowded. Watch for slugs and snails, the primary pests of hosta foliage, and provide consistent moisture through the growing season for the best leaf size and color.
sources: Missouri Botanical Garden Plant Finder — Hosta Cultivars

common_name: Forever Purple Heuchera (Deep Purple Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; morning sun deepens the purple foliage color while afternoon shade prevents scorch in hot climates.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade with protection from intense afternoon sun. Forever Purple, from Terra Nova Nurseries' Forever line, holds an intensely saturated, glossy dark purple leaf color from spring through fall better than many older purple heucheras, which tend to green out or fade in summer heat and humidity. Tiny white flowers appear on wiry stems above the compact foliage mound in late spring, but the season-long color consistency of the ruffled leaves is the main draw for edging, mass planting, and container use. Give it sharp drainage and even soil moisture, since heuchera dislikes both waterlogged crowns and drought stress, and divide congested clumps in early spring every three to four years to maintain vigor.

common_name: Dolce Cherry Truffle Heuchera (Chocolate-Cherry Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; morning sun deepens the rich chocolate-cherry foliage color.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade with some protection from hot afternoon sun. Dolce Cherry Truffle, part of Proven Winners' Dolce heuchera series, produces ruffled, glossy leaves in a rich chocolate-brown to deep cherry-red blend that shifts subtly with the seasons and light exposure, giving the compact mound a warm, dessert-toned color reminiscent of its name. Airy sprays of small white to pale pink flowers rise on thin stems above the foliage in late spring, drawing in pollinators. Like other heucheras it wants sharp drainage paired with consistent moisture, resents heavy, wet soil in winter, and benefits from division of crowded clumps every three to four years in early spring to keep the planting vigorous.
